# Colour literals tests/test_no_hex_literals_in_ui.py tolerates.
#
# ENTRY-GRANULAR, one per line:
#
#     <path>:<line>:<literal>  # reason
#
# A whole-file exemption is not expressible here on purpose (review F-6): a
# file-wide pass meant a new literal could hide behind an old one -- a
# 407-line UI page was exempt because of a single brand hex on line 43. The
# test asserts each scanned file's offences are EXACTLY the lines listed
# below, so a new literal fails even in a file that already has an entry,
# and a line that stops offending has to be deleted from this file.
#
# MASTER §4-3/§4-4 admits exactly one class of exception: a colour the DATA
# decides rather than the theme. Those live in core/theme.py's data_color()
# tables and are referenced by key from ui/, so they need no entry here.
#
# core/theme.py is exempt as the single OWNER of the token values -- that is
# not an exception to the rule, it is the rule (see OWNER_FILES in the test).

ui/pages/about_page.py:44:#5865F2  # Third-party BRAND glyph, inline SVG (Simple Icons, CC0): Discord blurple, the platform's own registered colour. A brand mark is not a theme decision -- recolouring it to an accent token would misrepresent the service the button links to.
ui/full_view_export.py:370:#22d3ee  # Avatar palette of the EXPORTED HTML document, cycled per character. Deliberately the document's own palette, not the app's tokens: a file exported yesterday must not look different from one exported today because the user changed theme in between. The document's stylesheet itself lives in assets/full_view/export.css, which the scanner does not read.
